title: From Snippet to Post: Why We Built Ananta Ideas
excerpt: The best ideas show up mid-scroll, not mid-writing-session. So we built a place to catch them.
bodyMarkdown:
Most of what ends up on this blog started as a half-formed thought while reading someone else's article, not as a deliberate sit-down-and-write session. The problem was never a shortage of ideas - it was that they evaporated by the time we had thirty free minutes to write.

So the workflow this site is built around is deliberately small:

1. **Capture** - a title, a raw snippet, a couple of tags, maybe a source link. Ten seconds, from a phone or a laptop.
2. **Compile** - later, with more time, turn one or several related ideas into an actual draft: title, slug, cover image, a Markdown body.
3. **Publish** - flip a switch in the app. A Supabase Edge Function renders the post and pushes it straight to this site's GitHub repo, which redeploys automatically.

> Capture fast, compile later, publish with one tap.

This post itself is the first thing that made it all the way through that pipeline. If you're reading it on blogs.theananta.in, the pipeline works.
